analysis: The PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md gains a paragraph (head lines 595-611) on a Gated DeltaNet four-row prompt kernel, and docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED row at line 1741. The supplied units cover other parts of inference.md (head lines 1644-2222) that the patch did not change. No code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization, or cache storage or crypto behavior changes in the visible diff. The new text claims the selected kernel reproduces gated_delta_step bit for bit and that mixing kernels across chunks cannot change the recurrent state used by checkpoint capture. That is a correctness and integrity claim for the prefix-cache path (T-041, A-001), and the underlying implementation (GatedDelta.swift) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. If the new kernel diverged numerically, cached checkpoints could be corrupted or inconsistent. That would be a correctness and availability concern rather than a confidentiality one. The kernel selection is per-process and picks a kernel only when it matches the stock kernel on a probe window. The env knob can only force the stock, packed or rows kernel and does not widen TTL, cache scope, lookup-tag derivation or the disk budget. The SSD tier's at-rest posture (HMAC names, DBK3 AAD, 30-minute TTL, salt scoping) is unchanged. The remaining unverified item is the actual GatedDelta.swift behavior, including that the bit-exact probe is sound and that a forced mode cannot bypass it. A reviewer of the code diff should check that. I found no concrete security regression in the supplied documentation.
